findings.title: Open-ended out-of-scope catch-all
findings.problem: The out-of-scope list ends with an open catch-all, so the boundary of what the assistant refuses is left to the model's judgement.
findings.proof: Out of scope: buying, paying, orders, accounts, discounts, messages, files, pictures; health, legal or money advice; anything else.
findings.fix: Replace 'anything else' with an explicit rule: any request not in the in-scope list gets the off_topic reply and an offer to search for a product instead.

findings.title: No rule for a shopper who may be a minor
findings.problem: The system prompt has no rule for a shopper who appears to be a minor, such as collecting age-appropriate handling or avoiding personal data from a child; the only age rule covers products for children under three.
findings.fix: Add a short section to the system prompt on how the assistant handles a self-described minor's messages, including no collection of personal data and no age-gated product claims.

findings.title: Spoken short forms missing for several declined categories
findings.problem: The spoken short-form list in fixed_replies.md has no entries for no_restricted, no_fabrication or no_unconfirmed, so a product answer that declines these parts has no spoken sentence for them.
findings.proof: Spoken before a product answer, these are shortened so that the reply still fits 15 seconds:
findings.fix: Add short-form versions of no_restricted, no_fabrication and no_unconfirmed to the spoken list in fixed_replies.md.

findings.title: Conflicting wording for empty table cells
findings.problem: The system prompt says an empty cell reads 'none is stated', while the knowledge file says 'not stated', so the Answerer and code may emit different text for the same case.
findings.proof: A cell holds a cited source's statement or says that none is stated.
findings.fix: Choose one fixed phrase for an unstated cell and use it in both the system prompt and catalog_and_sources.md.

findings.title: Tool-call caps for Planner and Retriever are not reconciled
findings.problem: The Planner is capped at three tool calls while the Retriever allows ten per turn with two added rounds, and the relationship between these caps is never stated.
findings.proof: a strategy and at most three tool calls with filters
findings.fix: State one per-turn ceiling and say whether the Planner's three calls count inside it or separately.

findings.title: Shopper message is not in a declared data fence
findings.problem: The fence list names only earlier turns, products on screen and tool results, so the raw shopper message re-read by the Router for a buried product request is not declared as data.
findings.fix: Add a <shopper_message> fence, declared as data never instructions, and apply it to every model that reads the transcript, including the second Router reading.

findings.title: No declared fence or sanitisation rule for the transcript
findings.problem: The context gives no rule that speech-recognition output is sanitised before a model reads it, so injected text in the transcript relies on the input screen's pattern matching alone.
findings.fix: Add a sentence stating that the transcript passes through the input screen and is fenced as data before any model reads it.

findings.title: Rag.search description carries policy prose
findings.problem: The rag.search description runs to several hundred tokens, restating the loosening order and under-three rule that the system prompt and code already enforce.
findings.proof: filters are loosened in this order until enough are found: claims, materials
findings.fix: Keep the description to what the tool does and when to call it, and move the loosening order into one place in the system prompt.

findings.title: Grounding corpus gives no sample tool output
findings.problem: catalog_and_sources.md describes product fields in prose but supplies no sample record or result, so the Answerer has no concrete example of the evidence shape it must cite.
findings.fix: Add one anonymised rag.search result and one web.search result to the knowledge corpus, labelled as sample data.

findings.title: Personal-details rule stated twice
findings.problem: The personal-details rule appears in the Safety policy and again in the code-enforced section with overlapping wording.
findings.proof: Names, addresses, e-mail addresses, phone, card and ID numbers are not needed to shop.
findings.fix: Keep the code-enforced placeholder rule and reference it from the Safety policy in one line.

findings.title: Catalog facts repeated across schema and knowledge file
findings.problem: The catalog's dataset name, product count and snapshot date are restated in both the rag.search description and the knowledge file.
findings.proof: Search the private product catalog (Amazon Product Dataset 2020; 9,740 products; listings and prices are a January 2020 snapshot)
findings.fix: Keep the dataset facts in the knowledge file only and remove them from the tool description.

findings.title: Short-form fixed sentences duplicate full forms
findings.problem: fixed_replies.md lists every spoken sentence twice, once in full and once in short form, and the short forms are the only ones spoken before a product answer.
findings.proof: Spoken before a product answer, these are shortened so that the reply still fits 15 seconds:
findings.fix: Keep one entry per reply id with a 'short' field instead of two parallel lists.

context_engineering.summary: The context is well organised, with clear pipeline stages, strong grounding and good injection controls, but it carries duplicated rules and a long tool description that waste tokens, and it leaves gaps for minors, short-form fixed replies and the shopper-message fence.

It has no accounts, no orders, no payments and no personal records; both tools are read-only.
metadata.goal: Recommend up to three products that fit what the shopper asked for, state only what the retrieved evidence states, cite a source for every product, keep the spoken reply short, refuse unsafe requests, and stay within product discovery.
